title: Enterprise Sales Kit: Positioning, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ (Q3 2026)
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Q3 2026 enterprise sales kit for Redwood Inference. It consolidates positioning and messaging, competitive briefing notes, recommended pitch-deck talking points, pricing guidance for sales conversations, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this asset for discovery calls, executive briefings, RFP responses, and partner enablement.

Audience
- Sales AE/SE motion: enterprise and platform buyers (SaaS/ML infra/IT)
- Solutions engineers and sales leadership
- Partner GTM and channel teams

1) Positioning and Messaging (60s elevator -> 5m executive brief)

Elevator (60s)
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that helps engineering teams ship LLM-powered features with production-grade latency, predictable unit economics, and flexible deployment modes (hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/VPC deployments). We make it simple to move from prototype to SLA-backed production without re-architecting model serving or sacrificing performance.

Core Messaging Pillars
- Production-first performance: 95th-percentile latency SLOs, GPU-optimized runtime, and continuous batching for cost-efficiency.
- Predictable economics: clear levers (batching, caching, quantization, routing) and transparent per-token & reserved capacity pricing.
- Deployment flexibility: one API and operational surface across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Reliability & controls: automatic fallbacks, canary rollouts, and enterprise-grade security (KMS, audit logs).

Target Personas & Talking Points
- Head of Product / ML Engineering: emphasize model life-cycle features (versioning, rollouts) and dev DX (SDKs, quickstarts).
- Infrastructure / Platform: emphasize capacity planning, reserved pools, autoscaling policies and cost controls.
- Security / Legal: emphasize private control plane, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and SOC/ISO evidence.
- Business Execs: ROI story - time-to-production, unit cost reduction, and uptime guarantees.

Objection handling (examples)
- "Why not build in-house?" -> Building and maintaining a high-throughput, economical inference stack is expensive and distracts teams from product differentiation; Redwood provides pre-tuned runtime, observability, and cost controls that pay back in months for typical production workloads.
- "What about model portability?" -> Same API and deployment abstraction across hosted/dedicated/private means customers can pin versions and move between modes without rewriting clients.

2) Competitive Briefs (one-page summaries for quick prep)

Competitive matrix (summary):
- Redwood Inference: unified runtime, cost-aware controls, flexible deployment modes, strong observability.
- Major Cloud AI Providers: broad managed services, easy to start, but less transparent unit economics and less flexible private/offline options.
- Self-hosted Inference Runtimes (open-source): greater control, but higher operational burden and longer time-to-production; fragmentation across kernels and orchestration.
- Inference specialty vendors: strong runtime performance but limited product surface or weaker enterprise controls/console.

Battlecard highlights vs. "Cloud A" (managed endpoint):
- Strengths: lower predictable cost for steady-state workloads (reserved), better on-prem and VPC options, deeper rollout/observability features.
- Weaknesses: smaller catalog of proprietary models (we emphasize curated open models + verified performance).
- Win themes: migrations from Cloud A for customers needing determinism, cost predictability, or private deployments; emphasize reference customers & performance benchmarks.

Competitive talking points vs. "Self-Serve Runtimes":
- Redwood reduces ops overhead (autoscaling, kernel selection, CVE/patch cadence) and provides SLA-backed Dedicated for enterprise customers.

3) Pitch Deck - Recommended Structure and Slide-by-Slide Talking Points

One-page TL;DR slide (what we are and why it matters)
- Bullet: Developer-first inference platform for production LLMs; reduces time-to-production and inference unit cost.

Problem slides (customer pain)
- Common points: high per-token cost, unpredictable tail latency, model/version sprawl, operational burden of serving at scale.

Solution slides (how Redwood solves it)
- Runtime optimizations, caching and batching, model catalog & quantization profiles, unified API, Dedicated & Private deployment options.

Customer outcomes (metrics to use)
- Example metrics: 40-60% reduction in per-token cost vs naive self-hosted setups; 30-60% improvement in 95th pctl latency after kernel and batching tuning; time to production reduced from months to weeks for cross-functional teams.

Commercials slide (short summary)
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation and per-embedding) with monthly minimum for enterprise tiers.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity pricing (monthly or annual commitments) with included support tier and predictable throughput.
- Private: licensing + professional services + optional support tier.

Call to action
- Recommended next steps: SE demo, small proof-of-value (2-4 week), architecture review, and procurement kickoff for Dedicated pilots.

4) Pricing Guidance (talking points & reference table)

Principles to follow in negotiation
- Be transparent: present trade-offs between hosted flexibility and Dedicated predictability.
- Anchor on business value: usage elasticity vs guaranteed throughput for product-critical flows.
- Use pilots: convert evidence from PoV into committed reserved capacity.

Reference pricing bands (Q3 2026, enterprise guidance - examples for sales conversations; final quotes from pricing team)
- Hosted API (developer/enterprise tier): generation: $0.0008 - $0.0030 per token (volume & model dependent); embeddings: $0.002 - $0.01 per embedding.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): monthly commitment per GPU-equivalent (v100/80GB or A100-class): $12,000 - $40,000 per GPU-eq/month depending on isolation, support, and region.
- Private / On-prem license: platform fee $150,000 - $400,000 base + professional services and optional support.
- Enterprise add-ons: extended observability retention, compliance packages, premium SLAs - priced separately.

Discounting guidance
- Use consumption minimums, committed terms (12/24/36 months) and pilots-to-commit milestones. Follow discount bands in Salesforce CPQ; escalate atypical requests to pricing@redwood.com.

5) Case Studies & Reference Stories (short one-paragraph summaries suitable for slides)

ACME Retail (e-commerce personalized search)
- Challenge: latency-sensitive reranking pipeline at peak traffic; high per-token cost and model sprawl across teams.
- Solution: Moved reranking to Redwood Dedicated with KV prefix caching and quantized model variants; applied routing policy for regional failover.
- Outcomes: 45% reduction in per-query inference cost, 220ms median -> 160ms P50 and 95th pctl improved 400ms -> 230ms; integrated into production in 6 weeks.

FinLedger (financial SaaS)
- Challenge: regulatory requirement for data residency and auditability for LLM features; needed private deployment in customer VPC.
- Solution: Private deployment with customer-managed control plane, KMS integration for keys, and enhanced audit logging.
- Outcomes: passed customer SOC readiness checks, time-to-production 10 weeks including compliance artifacts; enabled multi-tenant product with per-tenant routing.

HealthSym (enterprise healthcare platform)
- Challenge: maintain high inference quality while lowering inference cost for clinical note summarization workflows.
- Solution: Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization profile + intelligent batching) and continuous evals for quality guardrails.
- Outcomes: 55% cost reduction per inference, quality regressions detected pre-deploy via integrated evals.

6) Security FAQ (prospect-facing, short answers)

Q: Where is customer data stored and how is it isolated?
A: Data residency depends on deployment mode. Hosted customers select region-level storage; Dedicated and Private options provide tenant isolation. We support VPC peering and private networking for traffic separation.

Q: How do you manage encryption and keys?
A: We support TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. For Dedicated and Private, customers can integrate their KMS/HSM (Bring Your Own Key). Hosted customers may opt into managed KMS backed keys.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and access traces?
A: Yes. Audit logs are available as part of the platform and include request metadata, model/version used, and operator actions. Extended retention is an add-on.

Q: How do you prevent model/data leakage between tenants?
A: Tenant isolation is enforced at the network and runtime layer. KV caches and model variant stores are scoped per-customer in Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers use logical isolation with strict tenancy controls.

Q: Do you support attestations and compliance reports?
A: We provide SOC/ISO artifacts for enterprise contracts and work with customers to scope additional evidence. Private customers may run on-prem scans and independent audits.

Q: How are security incidents handled?
A: Incidents follow our security incident response process; customers receive timely notifications per their contract and can opt into post-incident reviews. Contact security-ops@redwood.com for escalation.

8) Recommended Playbook (operational steps for running a deal)
1. Discovery call: align on personas, workload characteristics (qps, seq length, latency SLOs), and security constraints.
2. SE deep-dive: architecture review and recommended deployment mode. Capture model sizes, concurrency, and token budget.
3. PoV/POC: propose 2-4 week PoV with success criteria (cost per 1k requests, 95th pctl latency, quality on eval set).
4. Procurement: confirm commercial terms, reserved capacity sizing if applicable, and compliance artifacts.
5. Onboarding & ramp: schedule onboarding, pilot review, and rollout plan with canary + rollback policy.
